reply_text:
I found one dated AI prediction by Sundar Pichai from 2017. It's in his own post on Google's blog on 17 May 2017, the day of the Google I/O keynote. He wrote that Google hopes AutoML will let "hundreds of thousands of developers" design their own neural networks "in three to five years". It's worded as a hope, not a firm forecast, which is worth knowing when you weigh it. Nothing from 2017 was already on your recorded list.

- **The I/O 2017 keynote (Singju Post transcript):** the page opened, but it was cut off partway through the event. In the part I could read, Pichai gave no other dated forecast. His one other forward-looking line, "I'm entirely confident one day AI will invent new molecules…", has no date and isn't about AGI, so I left it out. The line about adding Italian, Spanish and Korean to the Assistant by the end of the year was said by Scott Huffman, not Pichai.
- **Earnings calls:** the Q3 2017 transcript on fool.com opened but only had the finance chief's remarks, not Pichai's. The Q2 2017 transcript on roic.ai would not open. Pichai's 2017 earnings-call remarks are therefore not checked.
- **The founders' letter:** the one released in April 2017 was written by Larry Page, not Pichai, so it doesn't count.
- **Search budget:** my code crashed during the first fixed search, and I then ran fixed searches 2 and 3 separately. All three fixed searches ran once each. The search allowance ran out before my last search ran, so it is listed with "not run" below.
